footer: Records made with this tool do not guarantee legal effect. If you need an accredited timestamp (certified by Japan's Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications), please use an accredited provider.
h1: Record "when I published it" on a third-party ledger
lead: Send only the hash (fingerprint) of a text, photo or page and get a timestamp record. Your content is never uploaded. Free, no sign-up.
step1: 1. Choose a text or a file
ph_text: Paste text here (hashed inside your browser)
err_hash: Choose a text or file first.
err_rate: Rate limit reached. Please try again later.
how1: Your browser computes the SHA-256 and only the hash is sent. We never store your text or files. If you enter a page URL, our server fetches that public page once, keeps only its hashes and the URL (never shown publicly), and discards the content.
how2: You immediately get a signed time stamp (RFC 3161) from this service.
how3: It is also sent to OpenTimestamps public calendars and is anchored in a Bitcoin block within hours. After that it can be verified from the Bitcoin ledger alone, even if this service disappears.
faq1a: It is one piece of evidence on a third-party ledger that data matching this hash existed at the recorded time. It does not show that the content is true or who made it.
faq2a: No. Hashing happens inside your browser.
faq3q: What if I edit the article?
faq3a: Any change alters the hash, so record each revision (the WordPress plugin does it automatically).
st_pending: Accepted; waiting to be anchored in a Bitcoin block (usually within hours)
st_tsa_only: Signed time stamp only (Bitcoin submission being retried)
c_dl_note: Keep these; they let you verify without this service.
c_badge_note: A plain link. Use it only if you want to.
c_notfound: No record found for this ID.
v_lead: Choose data (a file or text) to look for records with the same hash. If you have .tsr / .ots files you can verify them too.
a_lead: An HTTP API that takes only a hash. No authentication; limited to 10/hour and 50/day per IP.
terms.what_p: DateSealed attaches a signed time stamp (RFC 3161) and a Bitcoin-ledger record (OpenTimestamps) to a SHA-256 hash that you send. It is a free tool operated by Lightscend Co., Ltd.
terms.not_p: A record is one piece of evidence that data matching the hash existed at the recorded time. It does not show that the content is true, who created it, or who holds the rights. Records made with this tool do not guarantee legal effect. If you need an accredited timestamp (certified by Japan's Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications), please use an accredited provider.
terms.store_h: What we store, and what we do not
terms.store_p: We store the hash, the record time, the signature serial number and the proof files (.tsr / .ots). If you use page URL input, we also keep the URL you entered (never shown on public pages) and the dates the page states about itself; the fetched content itself is discarded. We never receive or store your text or files. For rate limiting, IP addresses are kept only as salted hashes for 30 days and then deleted. We do not use cookies.
terms.ban_p: Automated bulk submission, interference with the service, and use intended to deceive others are not allowed. We may apply limits without notice.
terms.disc_p: The service is provided free, as is, and may change or end. Once a record is anchored in the Bitcoin ledger it can still be verified if this service closes.
terms.contact_p: Lightscend Co., Ltd. (contact details will be published soon).
api_note: The API reference is in English.
url_hint: We fetch the public page once and record two hashes: its main text and its raw HTML. The page content is discarded after hashing.
kind_url-text: Main-text hash of a web page
kind_url-raw: Raw-bytes hash of a web page
c_claims_h: Dates stated by the page itself
c_claims_note: Reference only. These are what the page claims about itself; DateSealed does not verify them.
terms.analytics_p: To count visits to our public pages we use Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics. Consent for cookies and advertising features is denied by default, so these tools run without setting cookies. They are not loaded on record pages (the addresses that contain a record ID) or in the API. Google may receive your IP address and the address of the page you view as part of this measurement.
fix_translation: Found an awkward translation? Help us fix it.
